title: Performance: fix the O(n^2) load; ordered index buckets
description:
Design §3.1. No behaviour change.

## Steps
1. `lookup_existing_record_from_load` (`table.rs`, around line 880) scans `record_keys` linearly for every file. Add a reverse `HashMap<key, filename>` so loading is linear. Check `_python/table.py` for the same pattern and fix it too.
2. Index buckets become ordered: `BTreeMap<(OrderedValue, pk), ()>` (reuse `sort.rs` ordering), so a query no longer clones and sorts the whole partition. Base tables get an ordered map over the primary key.
3. Add a benchmark example `rust/examples/load_bench.rs` (`cargo run --release --example load_bench -- 10000 50000`) that prints load and index-query times in `index_only` and `memory` modes.

## Acceptance
- `make check` green.
- 50k-record load time is at most 6× the 10k load time (roughly linear). Paste the numbers in a comment.

## Verify
`make check PYTHON=$PWD/.venv/bin/python`, then `cd rust && cargo run --release --example load_bench -- 10000 50000`.
